checklist.name: Royal Commission Case Study 40 — Australian Defence Force
Royal Commission Case Study 2 — YMCA NSW
The Forgotten Children — National Inquiry into Children in Immigration Detention (AHRC)

kinds.label: Religious institutions
kinds.definition: Sexual abuse of children by clergy, religious, lay leaders or members of a church, order, mosque, madrasa, temple, synagogue or other faith body, and the body's handling of it (transfers, secrecy, failure to report).
kinds.source: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse (Australia), Final Report, 15 Dec 2017, Volume 16 'Religious institutions'; Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse (England and Wales), investigation strands announced 2015-16 (Roman Catholic Church; Anglican Church; child protection in religious organisations and settings)

kinds.label: Cults, sects and closed communities
kinds.definition: Abuse inside high-control groups or separated communities (sects, communes, polygamous groups, closed colonies) where leaders control contact with outsiders, schooling and marriage, so abuse is hidden or authorised from within.
kinds.source: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse (Australia), Final Report, 15 Dec 2017, Volume 16 'Religious institutions' (closed faith communities); Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse (England and Wales), investigation strands announced 2015-16 (child protection in religious organisations and settings)

kinds.label: Children's homes, orphanages and residential care
kinds.definition: Abuse of children living in institutional care run by the state, a charity or a church: children's homes, orphanages, industrial and reformatory schools, shelters, residential treatment and 'troubled teen' programmes, past and present.
kinds.source: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse (Australia), Final Report, 15 Dec 2017, Volume 11 'Historical residential institutions' and Volume 12 'Contemporary out-of-home care'; Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse (England and Wales), investigation strands announced 2015-16 (Lambeth; Nottinghamshire councils; Cambridge House/Knowl View, Rochdale)

kinds.label: Foster and family-based state care
kinds.definition: Abuse of children placed by a state agency with foster, kinship or farm families (including Swiss Verdingkinder and Berlin's Kentler placements), and the agency's failure to check or remove them.
kinds.source: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse (Australia), Final Report, 15 Dec 2017, Volume 12 'Contemporary out-of-home care' (foster and kinship care)

kinds.label: Schools, boarding and residential schools
kinds.definition: Abuse by teachers or staff in day schools, boarding schools, residential schools for Indigenous children, schools for deaf or disabled children and religious schools, and the schools' handling of complaints.
kinds.source: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse (Australia), Final Report, 15 Dec 2017, Volume 13 'Schools'; Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse (England and Wales), investigation strands announced 2015-16 (abuse in state and independent residential schools)

kinds.label: Childcare and early-years services
kinds.definition: Abuse of young children in day care, crèches, preschools and out-of-school-hours care, where staff vetting, supervision and the handling of early warnings are at issue.
kinds.source: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse (Australia), Final Report, 15 Dec 2017, Report of Case Study 2 (YMCA NSW) and Volume 14 'Sport, recreation, arts, culture, community and hobby groups' / Volume 6 'Making institutions child safe'

kinds.label: Sport
kinds.definition: Abuse by coaches, team doctors, scouts or officials in clubs and national sports bodies, and the bodies' handling of complaints.
kinds.source: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse (Australia), Final Report, 15 Dec 2017, Volume 14 'Sport, recreation, arts, culture, community and hobby groups'

kinds.label: Scouting, youth, arts and hobby groups
kinds.definition: Abuse in scouting and guiding, church youth societies, holiday camps, choirs and other recreation, arts and hobby groups run for children.
kinds.source: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse (Australia), Final Report, 15 Dec 2017, Volume 14 'Sport, recreation, arts, culture, community and hobby groups'

kinds.label: Hospitals, psychiatric care and medical professionals
kinds.definition: Abuse of child patients by doctors, surgeons, psychiatric staff or people given access to hospitals, and the health bodies' handling of it.
kinds.source: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse (Australia), Final Report, 15 Dec 2017 (health and allied institutions examined, e.g. Tasmania; and Volume 6 'Making institutions child safe'); Lampard investigation of the NHS (2015) on Savile

kinds.label: Youth detention and custody
kinds.definition: Abuse of children held in juvenile halls, youth detention centres, training schools and secure units, by staff or with staff knowledge.
kinds.source: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse (Australia), Final Report, 15 Dec 2017, Volume 15 'Contemporary detention environments'; Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse (England and Wales), investigation strands announced 2015-16 (children in custodial institutions, incl. Medomsley)

kinds.label: Immigration detention and migrant children in state custody
kinds.definition: Sexual abuse or exploitation of children held in immigration detention, offshore processing or state-run shelters for unaccompanied migrant children, and children who go missing from reception into trafficking.
kinds.source: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse (Australia), Final Report, 15 Dec 2017, Volume 15 'Contemporary detention environments' (includes immigration detention)

kinds.label: Armed forces, military training and cadets
kinds.definition: Abuse of child recruits, apprentices and cadets inside military training establishments and cadet forces, and abuse of local children by service personnel stationed at bases, outside combat.
kinds.source: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse (Australia), Final Report, 15 Dec 2017, Report of Case Study 40 (Australian Defence Force) and Volume 15

kinds.label: Child migration programmes
kinds.definition: Children sent overseas by governments and charities under child migration schemes (e.g. UK to Australia, Canada, Rhodesia) who were sexually abused in the receiving institutions.
kinds.source: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse (England and Wales), investigation strands announced 2015-16 (child migration programmes, report 2018)

kinds.label: Entertainment, broadcasting and media
kinds.definition: Abuse by broadcasters, performers, talent agents, writers or modelling figures, using fame and access, and the employers' or industry's failure to act.
kinds.source: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse (England and Wales), investigation strands announced 2015-16 (and Dame Janet Smith Review for the BBC, 2016)

kinds.label: Politicians and public officials
kinds.definition: Abuse or exploitation by politicians, diplomats or officials, or their protection of offenders and obstruction of cases; includes allegations of elite rings that inquiries tested and found unsupported.
kinds.source: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse (England and Wales), investigation strands announced 2015-16 (allegations of child sexual abuse linked to Westminster; Cambridge House/Knowl View; Lord Janner)

kinds.label: Group-based grooming and exploitation networks
kinds.definition: Several offenders acting together who groom, pass around and sexually exploit children in a town or region, often targeting children in care; includes 'loverboy' recruitment.
kinds.source: Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse (England and Wales), investigation strands announced 2015-16 (child sexual exploitation by organised networks); Terminology Guidelines for the Protection of Children from Sexual Exploitation and Sexual Abuse (Luxembourg Guidelines; 1st ed. adopted Luxembourg 28 Jan 2016; 2nd ed. ECPAT/Interagency Working Group, March 2025), section H 'Solicitation of children for sexual purposes' (grooming)

kinds.label: Prostitution, brothels and paid sexual exploitation
kinds.definition: Children exploited for money or goods in brothels, bars, karaoke venues, mining camps, online sex advertising or 'compensated dating', by pimps, families or criminal groups.
kinds.source: Terminology Guidelines for the Protection of Children from Sexual Exploitation and Sexual Abuse (Luxembourg Guidelines; 1st ed. adopted Luxembourg 28 Jan 2016; 2nd ed. ECPAT/Interagency Working Group, March 2025), section E 'Exploitation of children in/for prostitution' and D.4.i 'Commercial sexual exploitation of children'

kinds.label: Travelling offenders and sexual exploitation in travel and tourism
kinds.definition: Offenders who travel or move abroad (as tourists, expatriates, volunteers or workers) to abuse children, and the tourism venues and states' responses (passport bans, notifications, deportations).
kinds.source: Terminology Guidelines for the Protection of Children from Sexual Exploitation and Sexual Abuse (Luxembourg Guidelines; 1st ed. adopted Luxembourg 28 Jan 2016; 2nd ed. ECPAT/Interagency Working Group, March 2025), section I 'Sexual exploitation of children in the context of travel and tourism'; Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse (England and Wales), investigation strands announced 2015-16 (children outside the United Kingdom)

kinds.label: Online abuse-material sites, forums and sharing networks
kinds.definition: Websites, darknet forums, messaging groups and peer-to-peer networks whose members share child sexual abuse material, and the platforms' and police responses.
kinds.source: Terminology Guidelines for the Protection of Children from Sexual Exploitation and Sexual Abuse (Luxembourg Guidelines; 1st ed. adopted Luxembourg 28 Jan 2016; 2nd ed. ECPAT/Interagency Working Group, March 2025), section F 'Child pornography / child sexual abuse material' and G.4.ii 'Child sexual exploitation online'; Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse (England and Wales), investigation strands announced 2015-16 (internet-facilitated abuse)

kinds.label: Commercial production and sale of abuse material
kinds.definition: Studios, producers and paid websites that make or sell abuse material for money, including 'model' studios and pay-per-view operations.
kinds.source: Terminology Guidelines for the Protection of Children from Sexual Exploitation and Sexual Abuse (Luxembourg Guidelines; 1st ed. adopted Luxembourg 28 Jan 2016; 2nd ed. ECPAT/Interagency Working Group, March 2025), section E.4.vii 'Use of children for pornographic performances' and section F

kinds.label: AI-generated and digitally altered abuse material
kinds.definition: Abuse material made or altered with software or AI, including 'nudified' or deepfake images of real children and training data containing abuse material.
kinds.source: Terminology Guidelines for the Protection of Children from Sexual Exploitation and Sexual Abuse (Luxembourg Guidelines; 1st ed. adopted Luxembourg 28 Jan 2016; 2nd ed. ECPAT/Interagency Working Group, March 2025), section F.4.ii 'Digitally generated child sexual abuse material'

kinds.label: Live-streamed abuse to order
kinds.definition: Abuse performed live on webcam for paying remote viewers, often arranged by adults close to the child, with payments through money-transfer services.
kinds.source: Terminology Guidelines for the Protection of Children from Sexual Exploitation and Sexual Abuse (Luxembourg Guidelines; 1st ed. adopted Luxembourg 28 Jan 2016; 2nd ed. ECPAT/Interagency Working Group, March 2025), sections G.4.iii 'Live online child sexual abuse', G.4.iv 'Live streaming', G.4.v 'Child sexual abuse to order' and G.4.vi 'Webcam child sex tourism'

kinds.label: Sextortion and online coercion networks
kinds.definition: Offenders or groups who obtain sexual images from children and then blackmail them for more images, money or self-harm, including organised groups such as 764 and the 'Com'.
kinds.source: Terminology Guidelines for the Protection of Children from Sexual Exploitation and Sexual Abuse (Luxembourg Guidelines; 1st ed. adopted Luxembourg 28 Jan 2016; 2nd ed. ECPAT/Interagency Working Group, March 2025), section H.4.iii 'Sexual extortion of children (sextortion)'

kinds.label: Grooming through games, chat and social platforms
kinds.definition: Adults contacting and grooming children through games, chat sites and social media, and the legal and regulatory action against the platforms.
kinds.source: Terminology Guidelines for the Protection of Children from Sexual Exploitation and Sexual Abuse (Luxembourg Guidelines; 1st ed. adopted Luxembourg 28 Jan 2016; 2nd ed. ECPAT/Interagency Working Group, March 2025), section H.4.i 'Grooming of children for sexual purposes' (online solicitation)

kinds.label: Cross-border trafficking for sexual exploitation
kinds.definition: Children recruited in one country and moved to another to be sexually exploited, by criminal groups, family networks or 'loverboys'.
kinds.source: Terminology Guidelines for the Protection of Children from Sexual Exploitation and Sexual Abuse (Luxembourg Guidelines; 1st ed. adopted Luxembourg 28 Jan 2016; 2nd ed. ECPAT/Interagency Working Group, March 2025), section K 'Trafficking of children'; UNODC Global Report on Trafficking in Persons (2022 and 2024 editions), forms of exploitation ('trafficking for sexual exploitation')

kinds.label: Trafficking for sexual exploitation within a country
kinds.definition: Children recruited and moved within their own country (from rural areas to cities, mining or tourist zones, or across state lines) to be sexually exploited.
kinds.source: Terminology Guidelines for the Protection of Children from Sexual Exploitation and Sexual Abuse (Luxembourg Guidelines; 1st ed. adopted Luxembourg 28 Jan 2016; 2nd ed. ECPAT/Interagency Working Group, March 2025), section K 'Trafficking of children' (no border crossing required); UNODC Global Report on Trafficking in Persons (2022 and 2024 editions), forms of exploitation (domestic trafficking flows)

kinds.label: Child and forced marriage used for sexual exploitation
kinds.definition: Girls married off, sold as 'brides', given in 'contract' or temporary marriages, or forced into 'marriage' by leaders or armed groups, where the marriage is the means of sexual exploitation.
kinds.source: Terminology Guidelines for the Protection of Children from Sexual Exploitation and Sexual Abuse (Luxembourg Guidelines; 1st ed. adopted Luxembourg 28 Jan 2016; 2nd ed. ECPAT/Interagency Working Group, March 2025), section L 'Child/early marriage'; UNODC Global Report on Trafficking in Persons (2022 and 2024 editions), forms of exploitation ('trafficking for forced marriages'); UNODC GLOTIP 2018 Booklet 2 (forced marriage by armed groups)

kinds.label: Illegal and fraudulent intercountry adoption
kinds.definition: Children sent abroad for adoption with falsified papers, without real parental consent or for payment, through agencies, notaries, orphanages or officials.
kinds.source: Terminology Guidelines for the Protection of Children from Sexual Exploitation and Sexual Abuse (Luxembourg Guidelines; 1st ed. adopted Luxembourg 28 Jan 2016; 2nd ed. ECPAT/Interagency Working Group, March 2025), section J 'Sale of children' (improperly inducing consent for adoption); UNODC Global Report on Trafficking in Persons (2022 and 2024 editions), forms of exploitation ('illegal adoption', 0.3% of detected victims in GLOTIP 2022)

kinds.label: Sale of babies, stolen newborns and 'baby factories'
kinds.definition: Newborns bought, stolen from maternity wards or bred in 'baby factories' and surrogacy operations, and sold to buyers at home or abroad.
kinds.source: Terminology Guidelines for the Protection of Children from Sexual Exploitation and Sexual Abuse (Luxembourg Guidelines; 1st ed. adopted Luxembourg 28 Jan 2016; 2nd ed. ECPAT/Interagency Working Group, March 2025), section J 'Sale of children'; UNODC GLOTIP 2020 (baby selling listed among forms detected)

kinds.label: Children taken by regimes and given false identities
kinds.definition: Children of detained, disappeared or 'undesirable' parents taken by a state or regime and placed with other families under falsified identities.
kinds.source: Terminology Guidelines for the Protection of Children from Sexual Exploitation and Sexual Abuse (Luxembourg Guidelines; 1st ed. adopted Luxembourg 28 Jan 2016; 2nd ed. ECPAT/Interagency Working Group, March 2025), section J 'Sale of children' (transfer of a child for consideration or any other advantage); UNODC Global Report on Trafficking in Persons (2022 and 2024 editions), forms of exploitation ('illegal adoption')

kinds.label: Abduction, recruitment and sexual slavery by armed forces and groups
kinds.definition: Children abducted or recruited by armed forces, militias, armed groups or gangs and used as fighters, 'wives' or sex slaves, or raped in conflict.
kinds.source: UNODC Global Report on Trafficking in Persons 2018, Booklet 2 'Trafficking in persons in the context of armed conflict' (recruitment of children; sexual slavery; forced marriage)

kinds.label: Peacekeepers and aid workers
kinds.definition: Sexual exploitation and abuse of children by UN and regional peacekeepers, international police and contractors, and humanitarian workers, often in exchange for food, money or aid.
kinds.source: UN Secretary-General's Bulletin 'Special measures for protection from sexual exploitation and sexual abuse' (ST/SGB/2003/13): sexual activity with anyone under 18 is prohibited

kinds.label: Customary and ritual servitude with sexual exploitation
kinds.definition: Children given to shrines, temples, households or powerful men under custom (trokosi, devadasi, bacha bazi, restavek, criadazgo, ngozi, ritual oaths), where sexual exploitation is part of the practice.
kinds.source: Terminology Guidelines for the Protection of Children from Sexual Exploitation and Sexual Abuse (Luxembourg Guidelines; 1st ed. adopted Luxembourg 28 Jan 2016; 2nd ed. ECPAT/Interagency Working Group, March 2025), sections E and J (exploitation and transfer of children under any arrangement); UNODC Global Report on Trafficking in Persons (2022 and 2024 editions), forms of exploitation ('other forms' of exploitation)

kinds.label: Orphanage trafficking and voluntourism
kinds.definition: Children recruited from families into orphanages (often 'paper orphans') to attract donations and foreign volunteers, where they are exposed to exploitation and sale.
kinds.source: Parliament of Australia, Joint Standing Committee on Foreign Affairs, Defence and Trade, 'Hidden in Plain Sight' (6 Dec 2017), Part 8: orphanage trafficking as modern slavery

kinds.label: Forced begging and forced criminality run by trafficking networks
kinds.definition: Children controlled by trafficking networks or exploitative schools and forced to beg, steal or commit crimes, often also exposed to sexual abuse.
kinds.source: UNODC Global Report on Trafficking in Persons (2022 and 2024 editions), forms of exploitation ('trafficking for begging'; 'trafficking for forced criminality')

cases.n: Australian Defence Force — HMAS Leeuwin, Balcombe and ADF Cadets (Royal Commission Case Study 40)
cases.victims_note: Defence Abuse Response Taskforce: allegations from more than 200 junior recruits aged 15-17 at HMAS Leeuwin alone
cases.who: Royal Australian Navy (HMAS Leeuwin), Army Apprentice School Balcombe, Australian Air Force Cadets
cases.cover: Senior staff at HMAS Leeuwin knew of the abuse and tolerated it; a 15-year-old cadet was disciplined and blamed after an adult instructor's relationship with her.
cases.d: The Royal Commission's Case Study 40 report (23 August 2017) found that physical and sexual abuse of child recruits was widespread at the navy base HMAS Leeuwin from the 1960s to 1972, that senior staff knew and tolerated it, and that the navy failed in its duty of care. At the Army Apprentice School, Balcombe, in the 1970s and 1980s an unofficial rank hierarchy let senior apprentices sexually and physically abuse junior ones. In the Air Force Cadets, policies from at least 2000 gave the age of consent as 14, which the commission said increased the risk of abuse. In June 2014 the Defence Abuse Response Taskforce had reported allegations from more than 200 junior recruits aged 15 to 17 at HMAS Leeuwin.
cases.cite: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, Report of Case Study No. 40 (Australian Defence Force), 23 Aug 2017; Minister for Defence statement on the DART report on HMAS Leeuwin, 18 June 2014

cases.n: UK cadet forces — 363 sexual abuse allegations in five years (BBC Panorama, MoD figures)
cases.who: Army Cadet Force, Air Training Corps and Sea Cadets (sponsored by the Ministry of Defence)
cases.cover: Former cadets and families told the BBC that officials discouraged them from going to the police.
cases.d: A BBC Panorama investigation in July 2017, using Freedom of Information figures from the Ministry of Defence, found 363 allegations of sexual abuse across the army, air and sea cadet forces between 2012 and 2017, both current and historical. Of these, 282 were referred to police and 99 adult instructors were dismissed. The programme reported that the MoD had paid more than £2 million to victims and that some victims and families had been urged not to tell police. The MoD said it had robust procedures and encouraged victims to report to police.
cases.cite: BBC Panorama (July 2017), reported by Forces News, 4 July 2017, citing MoD Freedom of Information figures

cases.n: YMCA NSW — Royal Commission Case Study 2 (Caringbah childcare worker Jonathan Lord)
cases.victims_note: SBS reported 12 boys; Australasian Leisure Management reported 13 children aged 6-11
cases.who: YMCA NSW (Caringbah out-of-school-hours care and holiday programmes)
cases.d: The Royal Commission's first hearing (October 2013) examined how YMCA NSW and police responded to 2011 allegations that childcare worker Jonathan Lord sexually abused children in its care at Caringbah; Lord was convicted and jailed with a minimum term of six years. The commission heard he was hired after improper reference checks and that staff did not pass concerns to senior management. Its 165-page report, published 2 July 2014, found staff training insufficient and YMCA NSW's policies deficient, and said the case 'calls into question the child safety practices of YMCA NSW'.
cases.cite: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, Report of Case Study No. 2 (YMCA NSW), 2 July 2014

cases.n: Amsterdam daycare abuse case (Het Hofnarretje) and the Gunning commission
cases.victims_note: charged with abusing 67 children; admitted abusing 87 (later reports say confessed to 83)
cases.who: Robert Mikelsons (childcare worker at Het Hofnarretje and Jenno's Knuffelparadijs) and his partner Richard van O.
cases.cover: An anonymous tip to Meld Misdaad Anoniem in 2008 was not acted on; the Gunning commission called it a missed opportunity.
cases.d: Childcare worker Robert Mikelsons abused babies and toddlers at two Amsterdam daycare centres and as a babysitter between February 2007 and January 2010. On 21 May 2012 the Amsterdam district court sentenced him to 18 years plus compulsory psychiatric detention (TBS); he was charged over 67 children and admitted abusing 87, and the appeal court raised the sentence to 19 years in April 2013. His partner Richard van O. was sentenced to six years. On 15 April 2011 a commission chaired by Louise Gunning-Schepers found that daycare centres, government bodies and others had failed, that risk signals were missed, and that a 2008 anonymous report had not been acted on.
cases.cite: Amsterdam District Court verdict, 21 May 2012 (DutchNews); Commissie-Gunning report, 15 April 2011 (AT5)

cases.n: Australia — 'The Forgotten Children': national inquiry into children in immigration detention
cases.place: Sydney (seat of the Australian Human Rights Commission)
cases.who: Australian Government immigration detention (onshore centres and Nauru regional processing centre)
cases.d: The Australian Human Rights Commission's national inquiry, 'The Forgotten Children', was tabled in Federal Parliament on 11 February 2015. It reported 33 incidents of reported sexual assault in immigration detention between January 2013 and March 2014, 'the vast majority involving children'. A separate government-commissioned review by Philip Moss (March 2015) on the Nauru centre was aware of three rape allegations, one involving a minor, and confirmed that a guard demanded to see a female detainee naked in exchange for extra shower time with her young child.
cases.cite: Australian Human Rights Commission, The Forgotten Children: National Inquiry into Children in Immigration Detention 2014, tabled 11 Feb 2015 (summarised in Medical Journal of Australia); Moss Review, March 2015 (Al Jazeera)

cases.n: United States — 4,556 sexual abuse complaints from unaccompanied migrant children in ORR shelters (2014-2018)
cases.place: Washington, D.C. (Office of Refugee Resettlement, HHS)
cases.who: Office of Refugee Resettlement (HHS) and contracted shelters for unaccompanied migrant children
cases.d: HHS records released in February 2019 by Rep. Ted Deutch showed 4,556 complaints of sexual abuse reported to the Office of Refugee Resettlement by unaccompanied migrant children in its care between October 2014 and July 2018. The Justice Department received 1,303 such complaints in fiscal years 2015-2018, of which 178 involved adult staff at the facilities. HHS said the figures were mischaracterised and that none of the allegations involved federal ORR staff.
cases.cite: HHS/ORR documents on sexual assaults FY2015-18, released by Rep. Ted Deutch, 26 Feb 2019 (CBS News)

notes:
Kinds list (35) merged from: (1) Australian Royal Commission final report volumes 11-16 (historical residential institutions; contemporary out-of-home care; schools; sport, recreation, arts, culture, community and hobby groups; contemporary detention environments; religious institutions) plus case studies 2 (YMCA) and 40 (ADF); (2) IICSA investigation strands (Westminster; Catholic Church; Anglican Church; internet; residential schools; Nottinghamshire; Lambeth; Janner; children outside the UK; custodial institutions; organised networks; Cambridge House/Knowl View; child migration; religious organisations and settings) - the IICSA site itself would not load, so the strand list was taken from ITV's report of the inquiry's August 2016 announcement; (3) Luxembourg Terminology Guidelines - only the 2nd edition (March 2025) PDF could be opened; its sections D-L (commercial sexual exploitation, prostitution, CSAM incl. digitally generated, technology-facilitated incl. live streaming/abuse to order, grooming, sextortion, travel and tourism, sale of children, trafficking, child marriage) match the 2016 first edition's structure, but section letters are cited from the 2nd edition; (4) UNODC GLOTIP 2022/2024 forms (sexual exploitation, forced labour, forced criminality, begging, forced marriage, illegal adoption, organ removal, mixed/other) and the 2018 Booklet 2 on armed conflict (child recruitment, sexual slavery, forced marriage). UNODC's own glotip page was blocked (permission prompt not answered); the 2022 and 2024 report PDFs were opened via INTERPOL and UN mirrors.
Kinds not taken directly from those four typologies, added because the brief listed them and the map holds many cases: peacekeepers and aid workers (sourced to the UN Secretary-General's bulletin on SEA, opened via UNDP; the UN conduct site was blocked), orphanage trafficking and voluntourism (Australian Parliament 'Hidden in Plain Sight', 2017), customary/ritual servitude (no typology names it as a category; mapped to Luxembourg E/J and UNODC 'other forms'), cults and closed communities (a sub-type of RC Vol 16 / IICSA religious settings).
Out of scope and not made into kinds: trafficking for organ removal; forced labour without sexual exploitation (e.g. gha-lake-volta-ijm-2023 left unassigned for that reason); children with harmful sexual behaviours (RC Vol 10); state removals without abuse or false identity.
Kinds that had fewer than 2 documented cases and were filled: armed forces and cadets (only jpn-okinawa-1995 before; added x-aus-adf-cs40-2017 and x-gbr-cadet-forces-2017); childcare/early years (only usa-mcmartin, which is 'disproved'; added x-aus-ymca-cs2-2014 and x-nld-amsterdam-daycare-2011); immigration detention and migrant children (only eur-europol-10000-missing-2016; added x-aus-forgotten-children-2015 and x-usa-orr-sexual-abuse-2019). Every other kind already had 2+ cases in 2+ countries.
Disproved or alleged cases are listed under kinds when they concern that kind (e.g. usa-mcmartin under childcare, gbr-operation-midland under politics) but were not counted toward the 2-case minimum.
Unconfirmed details: Jonathan Lord's victim count differs between sources (12 boys per SBS; 13 children aged 6-11 per Australasian Leisure Management) and his conviction year was not confirmed, so it is omitted. Who set up the Amsterdam Gunning commission was not confirmed, so that case is recorded as 'convicted' (court verdict) and is not added to the official-findings checklist. The UK cadet figures come from MoD FOI data reported by BBC Panorama via Forces News, not an official report, so status is 'reported'. The US ORR figures are HHS records released by a congressman (HHS disputed the framing), status 'reported', not a checklist item. The UNODC 2024 child shares by form were garbled in the copy opened and are not used.
Lead not pursued (kind already had 3 cases): Operation Golf (Met Police/Romanian police, Tandarei network; 181 Roma children trafficked to the UK to beg and steal; Romanian defendants acquitted on limitation grounds Dec 2019 - romania-insider.com) would strengthen forced begging/criminality.
